patients.summary: Construction worker and current smoker with COPD who joined in 2020; a 2022 low-dose CT found a small right lower lobe nodule, and in 2024 a right upper lobe mass proved to be stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab. Last seen 2025-05-09; outside records then show a COPD admission in 2025 and progression with SIADH in 2026, now on docetaxel.

conditions.note: On tiotropium since diagnosis by prior PCP

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43M, framer/carpenter on commercial crews, coming over from his old primary care office because his coworker is a member here and he wanted to be able to text a doctor. Came in at 7:30 so he could get to the site by 9.

COPD: told about two years ago by his last doctor after he got winded on ladders; did a breathing test then. On tiotropium capsule every morning and albuterol, uses the rescue maybe 2-3x a week, more in humid weather or around drywall dust. No ED visits, no steroid bursts he can remember. Mild morning cough, clear phlegm.

Tobacco: started at around 17, a pack and a half most days for years, now about a pack. Roughly 30 pack-years. Has tried cold turkey twice. Not interested in a quit date right now - 'it's the only break I get on the job.'
Alcohol: a few beers on weekends, not every weekend. No drugs.

PMH: COPD. PSH: none. Allergies: none known.
Family: father with COPD. Paternal uncle had lung cancer. No other family history he knows of.
Social: single, lives in Ludlow. Construction worker.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily, albuterol HFA 1-2 puffs q4-6h prn.

Exam: well appearing, talks in full sentences. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs: good air movement, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft. Ext: no clubbing, no edema. Skin: no lesions of concern.

A/P
1. COPD, on LAMA, symptoms controlled. Continue tiotropium and albuterol. Will get old records including his spirometry.
2. Tobacco use disorder. Advised quitting, offered patch/varenicline and quitline. Declined for now. Will revisit.
3. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, one-time hep C and HIV screen drawn today. Flu shot when the vaccine arrives.
RTC for physical in spring, sooner as needed. Records release signed.

documents.title: Your recent lab work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Derek - all of your bloodwork from last week came back normal: kidney and liver function, blood counts, sugar (A1c) and cholesterol are all fine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to do. We'll see you for your physical in the spring.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry. Good effort, acceptable and reproducible maneuvers. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 71% of predicted. No significant bronchodilator response.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory defect, consistent with COPD (moderate airflow limitation by FEV1).

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from the patient's previous primary care office, 23 pages, covering 2014 to 2020. Includes office notes, a 2018 spirometry report, medication list (tiotropium daily, albuterol as needed) and immunization history (influenza most years). No hospitalizations recorded. Scanned to chart and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old records. Spirometry May 2018: post-BD FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 71% predicted - fits his COPD diagnosis, moderate obstruction. Started on tiotropium after that. Smoking documented at every visit there. Nothing else outstanding. Problem list confirmed.

documents.title: Influenza vaccination
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came by after work for flu shot. No egg allergy, no prior reaction, feeling well today. Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 min, no issues.

documents.title: Refill: tiotropium
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for tiotropium 18 mcg capsules, 90-day supply. Last visit 08/2020, on med list. Pended to PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 44 y/o. Busy winter - indoor work on a renovation, says breathing has been about the same. Rescue inhaler a couple times a week. No exacerbations, no antibiotics this year. Still about a pack a day.

ROS otherwise negative: no chest pain, no weight change, no blood in sputum, no GI or urinary complaints, mood fine.

Meds: tiotropium daily, albuterol prn. NKDA.

Exam: NAD. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs with no wheeze or crackles today. RRR no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema, no clubbing. Skin ok.

A/P
- COPD: stable. Inhaler technique reviewed, good. Continue current regimen.
- Tobacco: discussed again. He knows. Not ready to pick a date. Offered meds - declined.
- Vaccines: PCV20 today given COPD and smoking; Tdap today (no record of one since his teens). He'll get his COVID shots at the pharmacy when his group opens.
- Labs today. Colon cancer screening starts at 45 - next year.
RTC 6 months for COPD check.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, your labs from Monday all look good - normal kidney and liver numbers, normal blood counts and a healthy cholesterol profile.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient sent a photo of his vaccine card through the portal. Pfizer COVID-19 primary series at a retail pharmacy: dose 1 on 4/14/2021, dose 2 on 5/5/2021. Entered into immunization history.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - COPD
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6-mo COPD check. Summer was hot and he was roofing for part of it; used albuterol more on the worst days, maybe daily for a stretch in July, back to 2-3x/week now. No fevers, no change in sputum, no ED or urgent care. Still smoking about a pack. Asked about vaping as a way to cut down - we talked through it; he hasn't tried.
O: Vitals as charted, sat fine on room air. Lungs: no wheeze, no crackles. No edema.
A/P: COPD, stable, no exacerbations. Continue tiotropium + albuterol. Heat/dust on site are his triggers - mask with a real respirator rating when cutting or sanding.
Tobacco: brief counseling again, quitline card given. Precontemplative.
Flu shot next month. Physical in March.

documents.title: Influenza vaccination
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine given IM right deltoid, lot and expiration logged. Tolerated well. Patient declined the COVID booster today, says he may get it at the pharmacy later.
